title: Agent runtime
description: Architect, developer and reviewer run as separate phases with deterministic verification in between. Pick a provider per role; everything else has a working default.
loadFailed: Could not load runtime settings. Retry before making changes.
unavailable: This Core installation does not include the agent runtime. Update Core before enabling it; you can prepare settings while disabled.
approvalBeforeArchive: Pause for approval before completing the workflow

providers.title: Providers
providers.hint: CLI providers use their existing login. API providers accept an environment variable name only, never an API key. Local endpoints can leave it blank. Assign another provider to a role before removing its current provider.
providers.globalHint: Two kinds of provider power every project: coding CLIs detected on this machine and local OpenAI-compatible engines you register here. Assign them to the pipeline phases in Project settings ▸ Agent engine. Changes apply to new executions.
providers.label: Display name (optional)
providers.noModels: No models discovered yet — test the connection.
providers.ratesHint: Costs are shown as estimates; leave both empty and cost stays unknown.
providers.ratesInvalid: Enter both rates as non-negative numbers, or leave both empty.
providers.reasoningEffortHint: Sends the OpenAI reasoning_effort field: the role's configured effort on every call, raised to high while the Compact architect writes the plan. Leave off unless the server honours it.
providers.apiKeyEnvMissing: {{name}} is not set in the app process. Set it in the environment the app is launched from.
providers.renameHint: Renaming keeps role assignments pointing at this connection.
providers.idLocked: The id is locked once saved. Use Rename to change it.
providers.empty: No connections yet. Add a local / API provider to get started.
providers.fixBeforeSave: Fix the highlighted fields before saving.
providers.agentLoopHint: how the implement pipeline drives this model
providers.agentLoop_compactHint: Host-driven micro-steps with structured output. Recommended for models under ~30B.
providers.agentLoop_freeHint: One agentic loop per role, like a CLI provider. Needs a strong model.
providers.contextWindowHint: Match the server's context size (n_ctx / num_ctx). Used to compact old tool results before the window fills. Default 32768.
providers.maxOutputHint: max_tokens of one tool turn; a turn cut off by it is retried once at double. Counts inside the context window, so it is always capped to the room left — raise it when the model thinks privately (thinking counts against it). Default 8192.
providers.reasoningEffortRailHint: Off: the reasoning-effort selector is hidden in the rail header for this engine.
providers.presetSmallModelHint: Sets Compact loop, forwards reasoning effort and a 32k context window — the combination validated with 7–14B models. You can still change each field.
providers.cliGroupHint: Detected on this machine — they use their own login, nothing to configure.
providers.localGroupHint: OpenAI-compatible endpoints (llama.cpp, Ollama, vLLM, LM Studio…) reachable from this app.
providers.emptyLocalPitch: No local engine yet. Point the app at an OpenAI-compatible endpoint to run the pipeline on your own hardware — cost stays under your control and nothing leaves your network.

agents.title: Role assignments
agents.hint: Each role can use a different provider and model. Manage connections in General settings → AI providers. Default limit: {{turns}} turns per agent.
agents.thinkingHint: Off by default: hidden reasoning spends the output budget and minutes per turn in a host-driven loop. Turn it on for a role that benefits from deliberation (sent as chat_template_kwargs.enable_thinking; ignored by endpoints that do not know it).

limits.title: Workflow limits
limits.hint: Empty fields use Core defaults: {{attempts}} correction attempts and {{minutes}} minutes per role step. On local engines the timeout applies to each unit of work (a task group, an artifact, a review) — 45 minutes by default — plus a 20-minute idle watchdog; a step that runs out of time blocks the run and can be resumed from the next open task group. Token and USD caps are optional; USD caps require Claude for every AI role.
limits.timeoutMinutes: Timeout in minutes (default {{minutes}}; local engines 45 per task group)

verification.title: Verification commands
verification.hint: Optional. These run after the developer finishes and their failures go back to the developer. Leave the list empty and the architect proposes the project's own checks on each run; repositories without any automated check are still reviewed.
verification.detected: Filled in from the checks this project already defines.
verification.nothingDetected: No test, type-check or build command was found. That is fine: the architect proposes checks at run time when possible.
verification.detectFailed: Could not inspect the project repositories.
verification.invalidLine: Verification command is empty or has an unterminated quote: {{line}}
verification.label: Check label (optional)

runs.title: Saved executions
runs.hint: Continue in the original worktree with the frozen scope and settings; progress appears in that job's log. This does not publish or restart Desktop delivery. Active rail executions are stopped from their job controls.
runs.question: The architect asks:
runs.answerPlaceholder: Answer the question; the architect continues with it.
runs.preserveProgress: Continue from the indicated phase, preserving your existing work and saved settings.
runs.reviewDelivery: Implementation completed. Review the result in this job log before arranging delivery; this continuation has not published it.
runs.selectRecovery: Select the interrupted attempts to recover

roleHints.architect: Reads the code and writes the proposal, design, tasks and spec. Read-only.
roleHints.developer: Implements the tasks with tests. Can edit files and run commands inside the CLI sandbox.
roleHints.reviewer: Checks the result against the spec and the verification evidence. Read-only.

review.title: Review gate
review.hint: Empty fields use Core's gate. Values can only raise it: overall score at least {{score}}, security at least {{security}}, other aspects at least {{aspect}}.

architect.title: Architect confidence
architect.hint: After one autonomous investigation pass, a design that is still low in confidence either pauses with the architect's question or proceeds on stated assumptions.

metrics.title: Usage and time
metrics.hint: Includes corrections and failed calls. Agent time includes tool work. Cached tokens are part of input tokens.
metrics.partial: Some attempts have no detailed measurements.

prompts.title: Agent role prompts
prompts.description: View and edit the instructions for each role. Shared by all projects and providers; changes apply to new jobs. Resumed jobs keep their original prompts.
prompts.contracts: Spec context, OpenSpec workflow and required response format are added automatically and are not edited here.
prompts.invalid: Each definition must contain 1–20,000 characters, with nonblank text and no null bytes.
prompts.fixerHint: Used on correction rounds only — after a failed verification or a rejected review. Runs on the developer's engine unless Settings ▸ Agent engine ▸ Fixer names its own. A CLI provider that resumes the developer's session receives the short correction follow-up instead; the definition applies whenever a fresh session starts (local engines, the fixer engine, a lost session).

efficiency.title: Implementation efficiency
efficiency.scope: Applies to new runs. Saved runs retain their original configuration and runtime.
efficiency.unknownSupport: Support is not confirmed for this model and transport. Provider default remains available.
efficiency.escalation: Allow one higher tier with the same provider
efficiency.baseRequired: Select an explicit base model first.

triggers.architect: Only the existing deeper investigation pass can select this tier.
triggers.developer: After two failed candidates, the next permitted attempt can select this tier.
triggers.reviewer: Only a malformed-response repair can select this tier; rejecting code does not trigger it.
triggers.fixer: Only a correction round can reach this tier; first passes never run the fixer.

efficiency.developerChecks: Accept additional checks proposed by the developer
efficiency.concurrencyHint: Default 1. Only host-declared independent checks across different repositories may run together. Checks are never reused by default.
efficiency.capabilitiesFailed: Could not confirm model capabilities. Update the paired Core runtime or keep provider defaults.

evidence.title: Verification evidence
evidence.unavailable: Evidence is unavailable for this execution. Its recorded outcome is not proof of current validity.
evidence.truncated: This is a bounded page or a truncated capture.
evidence.reuseConfirmed: Reused after verifying matching inputs and toolchain.
evidence.inputsChanged: Inputs changed during verification; result invalidated.
evidence.reuseUnproven: No current result with proven matching inputs; the check ran again.

loopRoles.title: Loop roles
loopRoles.hint: Engines for the loop-side roles when a rail launches with the "Roles" engine. The pipeline roles above (architect, developer, reviewer) already come from this runtime configuration.
loopRoles.verifierHint: Every non-core AI step of the loop: verify, fix and custom AI steps.
loopRoles.deciderHint: The Loop Decider that reads the verdict and routes the next step — a cheap, fast model is the natural pick.
loopRoles.disabled: The agent runtime is disabled — rails launched with the "Roles" engine are refused until it is enabled.
loopRoles.saveFailed: Could not save the loop roles.

pipeline.title: Implement pipeline
pipeline.explainer: These phases run in this order on every implementation. When the rail's engine is "{{roles}}", each phase runs on the engine configured below — a different provider, model and effort per phase. Picking a concrete engine on the rail runs every phase on that engine instead.

core.title: Core pipeline
core.hint: Runs inside every implement: plan, build, verify, fix, review.

loop.title: Loop steps
loop.hint: AI steps of the rail's loop around the run (verify → decide → fix) and of custom loops; they inherit the primary engine unless set.

architect.name: Architect
architect.purpose: Reads the code and writes the proposal, design and tasks.

verification.name: Verification
verification.purpose: The host runs your checks; failures go back to the developer.

fixer.name: Fixer
fixer.purpose: Corrects what verification or review reject; inherits the developer when not configured.

reviewer.name: Reviewer
reviewer.purpose: Checks the result against the spec and the evidence.

verifier.name: Verifier
verifier.purpose: Verify, fix and custom AI steps of the loop.

decider.name: Decider
decider.purpose: Reads the verdict and routes the next loop step.

fixer.title: Fixer engine
fixer.hint: Runs only on correction rounds — after a failed verification or a rejected review; first passes stay on the developer. A stronger or cloud model here pays off when the developer is a cheap local model.

guardrails.title: Guardrails
guardrails.intro: Process rules the host applies around local models so a small model does not derail. All on by default; switch one off only to tune the process. CLI providers are never affected.
guardrails.unsupported: This Core installation does not expose configurable guardrails. Update Core to tune them; the built-in rules still apply.
guardrails.unknown: A guardrail added by a newer Core; this app has no description for it yet.

plan-validation.title: Validated task plan
plan-validation.description: Rejects plans that target openspec/, list bare file names as tasks, have too few tasks/groups for the spec, or leave acceptance criteria uncovered; the architect retries.
plan-validation.why: A vague or incomplete plan is the #1 reason a small developer model writes stubs.

genuine-blocking-question.title: Only real blocking questions
genuine-blocking-question.description: The architect can pause the run only with an actual question ending in '?', never with copied example text.
genuine-blocking-question.why: Small models echo prompt placeholders and would block every run.

plan-language-hint.title: Plan in the repository's language
plan-language-hint.description: Tells the architect the primary language so task file names carry the right extension.
plan-language-hint.why: A JS plan on a TypeScript repo makes tasks impossible to tick.

frozen-plan-writes.title: Planning artifacts are frozen
frozen-plan-writes.description: The developer cannot write under openspec/; the plan is the host's.
frozen-plan-writes.why: Models 'implement' by editing the plan instead of the code.

primary-language.title: Primary language reminder
primary-language.description: Each task group is told the repository's primary language; new files should use it.
primary-language.why: Prevents a second implementation in another language.

duplicate-sibling.title: No twin modules across languages
duplicate-sibling.description: Refuses board.js when board.ts already exists; extend the existing module instead.
duplicate-sibling.why: Twins compile both and the tests import the wrong one.

one-test-per-module.title: One test file per module
one-test-per-module.description: Refuses board.tick.test.ts when board.test.ts exists; extend it instead.
one-test-per-module.why: Correction passes otherwise add a new suite per attempt.

empty-write.title: No empty overwrites
empty-write.description: An empty write over a populated file is refused; write the full content or patch it.
empty-write.why: A 'cleanup' pass once left index.ts at 0 lines.

evidence-gated-ticking.title: Evidence before ticking a task
evidence-gated-ticking.description: A task naming files is done only when they exist and are not stubs (sibling extensions accepted).
evidence-gated-ticking.why: Without it 'done' is just a claim and verify runs against nothing.

inventory-retry.title: Retry with the real inventory
inventory-retry.description: When the model gives up claiming the repo is empty while it is not, retry once with the file list.
inventory-retry.why: Cheap second chance instead of a failed step.

synthetic-corrections.title: Turn feedback into tasks
synthetic-corrections.description: When every task is ticked but review/verify failed, the feedback becomes concrete correction tasks.
synthetic-corrections.why: Otherwise the developer reports 'already done' and nothing changes.

silent-group-closure.title: Close silent groups, keep their files
silent-group-closure.description: A group whose model stops answering is closed with the files it wrote credited and its tasks left open, instead of failing the run.
silent-group-closure.why: A 9B model wrote five modules, went silent, and the whole run failed.

environment-repair.title: Host repairs the environment
environment-repair.description: Missing dependencies or test tooling (npm install, ts-jest, @types/jest, Jest config modules) are installed by the host, then verify re-runs once.
environment-repair.why: The model cannot fix the environment and burns corrections trying.

lockfile-repair.title: Drop hand-written lockfiles
lockfile-repair.description: A package-lock.json the model invented (EINTEGRITY/ETARGET) is removed and the install retried once.

verify-idle-timeout.title: Stop hanging tests
verify-idle-timeout.description: A verification command with no output for 5 minutes is stopped and reported as a probable hang (last output included).
verify-idle-timeout.why: A while-loop in a test otherwise holds the run until the 15-minute wall clock.

verify-per-group.title: Verify after each group
verify-per-group.description: Runs the repository's own test command right after each task group; a failure gets one in-place fix round while the group's context is still fresh.
verify-per-group.why: Five broken suites at the end are much harder to fix than one at a time.

test-reachability.title: Every new test must actually run
test-reachability.description: A test file the developer writes that the repository's test command never executes (an enumerating `test` script that skips the new file) fails verification with the exact file, at group altitude first and again at the host verify.
test-reachability.why: A 622-line test suite with six failing cases once shipped green because nothing ever ran it.

exit-code-honesty.title: Distrust a green exit code that reports failures
exit-code-honesty.description: A verification command that exits 0 while its output prints failures (`FAIL:` lines, "3 failed", an AssertionError) is treated as FAILED and handed to the fixer with the harness named as the defect.
exit-code-honesty.why: A hand-rolled test runner that never sets a non-zero exit code once shipped three red tests as green.

customRoles.title: Custom roles
customRoles.hint: Declare reusable instructions and explicit permissions for workflow roles.
customRoles.unsupported: Update Core to edit custom roles.
customRoles.invalidId: Use a unique lowercase ID beginning with a letter, up to 64 letters, digits or hyphens. Built-in IDs are reserved.
customRoles.escalationHint: Only a permitted protocol repair may use the escalation model. No extra retry is added.

steering.title: Run instructions
steering.hint: Core saves these instructions for the next eligible agent turn. Sending does not answer a question or grant approval.
steering.label: Additional instructions
steering.failed: Could not send instructions. Retry to confirm the same message.
steering.unreported: This Core version does not report consumption.
steering.truncated: Only the most recent receipts and pending messages are shown.

studioRole.title: Core role defaults
studioRole.hint: These file defaults apply to new workflows. Explicit project settings take precedence; saved runs keep their frozen settings.
studioRole.invalid: Fix the YAML frontmatter in the editor before changing role fields.
